argentina/recoleta-cemetery.name: Recoleta Cemetery
argentina/recoleta-cemetery.description: An ornate necropolis of mausoleums in the heart of Buenos Aires, the resting place of Eva Peron.
argentina/recoleta-cemetery.details: Recoleta Cemetery is a maze of marble tombs, statues and narrow lanes, and a showcase of the city history. The Duarte family vault holds Eva Peron. Free guided tours are offered in English at set times. The neighbourhood has a Sunday craft fair, cafes and the Basilica of Our Lady of the Pilar.

argentina/plaza-de-mayo.name: Plaza de Mayo and Casa Rosada
argentina/plaza-de-mayo.description: The historic main square, with the pink presidential palace, the cathedral and the Cabildo.
argentina/plaza-de-mayo.details: Plaza de Mayo has been the centre of Argentine political life since colonial times. The Casa Rosada is the presidential palace, and the Metropolitan Cathedral holds the tomb of General San Martin. The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo still walk on Thursday afternoons. Free palace tours run on weekends, and need registration.

argentina/san-telmo.name: San Telmo market and tango
argentina/san-telmo.description: A cobbled barrio of antique shops, Sunday market stalls and old milongas.
argentina/san-telmo.details: San Telmo is the oldest barrio of Buenos Aires, with colonial buildings and a Sunday street fair on Defensa. Tango dancers perform in Plaza Dorrego. Evening milongas and tango shows are held in historic halls nearby. The cobbled streets are uneven.

argentina/la-boca.name: La Boca and Caminito
argentina/la-boca.description: A colourful port neighbourhood with painted houses, tango and the Boca Juniors stadium.
argentina/la-boca.details: La Boca grew around Italian immigrant dockworkers and is known for the corrugated-metal houses painted in bright colours along the Caminito. Stay on the tourist streets and take care with belongings. The Boca Juniors stadium and museum are close, and match tickets are hard to get.

argentina/tango-show.name: Tango show and dinner
argentina/tango-show.description: An evening of live tango music and dance in one of the historic halls.
argentina/tango-show.details: Buenos Aires is the home of tango, and there are shows in grand old theatres with or without dinner. Choose between polished stage productions and more intimate milongas where locals dance. Dinner begins late, around nine, and the show can last two hours. Book ahead.

argentina/san-antonio-de-areco.name: San Antonio de Areco gaucho day
argentina/san-antonio-de-areco.description: A day trip to a village of gaucho tradition, an estancia lunch and horse riding.
argentina/san-antonio-de-areco.details: San Antonio de Areco is a small town about 90 minutes from Buenos Aires, known for gaucho crafts and its leather and silver workshops. Many estancias offer an asado lunch, folk music and horseback demonstrations. It is a good way to see the pampas on a day away from the city.

argentina/iguazu-argentine-side.name: Iguazu Falls, Argentine side
argentina/iguazu-argentine-side.description: A system of 275 waterfalls reached by boardwalks, including the Devil Throat.
argentina/iguazu-argentine-side.details: The Argentine side of Iguazu has the most extensive walkways, with the Upper and Lower circuits and a train to the Devil Throat viewpoint, where the water plunges into a huge gorge. Allow a full day. Rain can raise the river level and close some trails. Boat rides to the base of the falls can be added.

argentina/iguazu-brazil-side.name: Iguazu Falls, Brazilian side
argentina/iguazu-brazil-side.description: Panoramic views of the whole falls from the Brazilian side, a half-day visit.
argentina/iguazu-brazil-side.details: The Brazilian side gives sweeping views of the falls from a walkway, with a close approach to the Devil Throat from below. It takes about three hours and is usually combined with a transfer across the border. Bring your passport, and check visa rules for crossing into Brazil.

argentina/perito-moreno.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
argentina/perito-moreno.description: A huge advancing glacier that calves ice into Lago Argentino, seen from walkways or by boat.
argentina/perito-moreno.details: The Perito Moreno Glacier is about 30 kilometres from El Calafate in Los Glaciares National Park. A network of walkways faces the ice wall, where blocks crash into the lake with a thunderous roar. Boat trips run along its face, and guided ice trekking is available. Dress warmly, as it is cold and windy.

argentina/glacier-boat.name: Upsala and Spegazzini glacier cruise
argentina/glacier-boat.description: A full-day boat trip through icebergs to the glaciers on the northern arms of Lago Argentino.
argentina/glacier-boat.details: The cruise leaves from Puerto Bandera and passes icebergs to the Upsala and Spegazzini glaciers. Time ashore lets you walk to a viewpoint. It is a long day on the water, and the wind is cold. Book ahead.

argentina/el-chalten-hikes.name: El Chalten and Fitz Roy hikes
argentina/el-chalten-hikes.description: Hiking capital of Argentina, with day walks to Laguna de los Tres and Laguna Torre under Fitz Roy.
argentina/el-chalten-hikes.details: El Chalten sits below Mount Fitz Roy, and trails start at the edge of town. The walk to Laguna Torre is moderate and takes about six hours, while the Laguna de los Tres trail is harder and about nine hours. Weather changes quickly, and the summit is often in cloud, so keep a spare day.

argentina/mendoza-wineries.name: Mendoza and Uco Valley wineries
argentina/mendoza-wineries.description: Malbec cellars under the Andes, with tastings, lunch and vineyard views.
argentina/mendoza-wineries.details: Mendoza is the capital of Argentine wine. The wineries of Lujan de Cuyo and the Uco Valley offer tastings and long lunches with views of the Andes. Many places need reservations. Hire a driver or join a tour, and consider cycling in Maipu for an easier day.

argentina/aconcagua-high-andes.name: High Andes and Aconcagua viewpoint
argentina/aconcagua-high-andes.description: A mountain road day from Mendoza to Puente del Inca and a viewpoint of Aconcagua.
argentina/aconcagua-high-andes.details: The road to Chile rises through red and ochre canyons to Puente del Inca, a natural rock bridge over a hot stream, and the Aconcagua Provincial Park viewpoint. Aconcagua is the highest peak in the Americas. A day trip takes about nine hours, and altitude is noticeable.

argentina/bariloche-circuito-chico.name: Circuito Chico and Lake Nahuel Huapi
argentina/bariloche-circuito-chico.description: A scenic loop of lakes, viewpoints and chocolate shops near Bariloche.
argentina/bariloche-circuito-chico.details: Circuito Chico is a 60-kilometre loop west of Bariloche, passing Llao Llao, Lake Moreno and chairlift viewpoints at Cerro Campanario. Many people drive or take a tour. In winter the area is a ski resort, and in summer it is good for hiking, boating and kayaking. Bariloche is also known for chocolate.

argentina/cerro-catedral.name: Cerro Catedral or lake cruise
argentina/cerro-catedral.description: Mountain gondola or a boat trip on Lake Nahuel Huapi to Isla Victoria.
argentina/cerro-catedral.details: Cerro Catedral has chairlifts and gondolas with views in summer and skiing in winter. Boat excursions on Lake Nahuel Huapi visit Isla Victoria and the Arrayanes forest. Choose by weather, and carry layers.
